title: Memory retrieval preference helpers can throw on storage access failures
reasoning: The memory retrieval preference helpers call getItem and setItem on the resolved storage object without the try/catch protection used by configStorage. Browser storage operations can throw, for example when storage is unavailable, disabled, or quota/security policies reject access. That turns a non-critical preference read or write into a renderer exception instead of falling back to the default enabled value or returning the normalized setting.
recommendation: Wrap storage getItem/setItem calls in try/catch. Reads should return the safe default true when storage fails, and writes should return the normalized preference while optionally logging a warning.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature, and there is no evidence of a fake storage object that throws on getItem or setItem.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add unit tests using a storage stub whose getItem and setItem throw, asserting getMemoryRetrievalInjectionEnabled returns true and setMemoryRetrievalInjectionEnabled returns the normalized boolean without throwing.
minimumFixScope: Update memoryRetrievalPreference.js to handle storage exceptions for both read and write paths.
